# User profile linking migration (2026-01-31 16:12Z)

_**User**_

Create a new migration that links the user row to a profile row. You will be matching based on the currently logged in user email, uid in user table row and work_email in profile table row. Make sure this runs every time a user changes their email

---

_**Agent (model composer-1, mode Agent)**_


Reviewing the current schema to understand the user and profile tables before creating the migration.

        "contents": "-- Migration: Initial schema setup\n-- Purpose: Creates complete database schema with tables, triggers, and restrictive RLS policies\n-- Affected tables: users, profiles, teams\n-- Special considerations: All RLS policies are restrictive - admin operations require service_role or application-level checks\n\n-- ============================================================================\n-- ENUM TYPES\n-- ============================================================================\n\ncreate type public.profile_role as enum ('student', 'team_leader', 'coach', 'admin');\n\n-- ============================================================================\n-- TABLES\n-- ============================================================================\n\n-- Create users table (custom table, separate from auth.users)\n-- Stores Google OAuth user data and OTP tracking\n-- Linked to auth.users via auth_user_id for authentication checks\ncreate table public.users (\n  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),\n  auth_user_id uuid unique references auth.users(id) on delete cascade,\n  google_email text not null unique,\n  suggested_work_email text,\n  google_profile_picture text,\n  google_full_name text,\n  last_otp_sent_at timestamptz,\n  created_at timestamptz default now() not null,\n  updated_at timestamptz default now() not null\n);\n\ncomment on table public.users is 'Custom users table storing Google OAuth user data and OTP tracking.         "contents": "Use MODDATETIME extension to set the &#96;updated_at&#96; column on every update.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\n-- Users table to sync with auth.users (Google OAuth)\n-- Note: Synced via Next.js server actions, not database triggers\ncreate table public.users (\n  id uuid primary key references auth.users(id) on delete cascade,\n  email text not null,\n  name text,\n  picture text,\n  created_at timestamptz default now() not null,\n  updated_at timestamptz default now() not null\n);\n\n-- Role enum for profiles (authorization)\ncreate type public.profile_role as enum ('student', 'team_leader', 'coach', 'admin');\n\n-- Profiles table (pre-created by admin, linked to user after verification)\n-- Focus: Authentication and authorization only\ncreate table public.profiles (\n  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),\n  name text not null,\n  user_id uuid unique references public.users(id) on delete set null,  -- linked after OTP verification\n  work_email text unique not null,\n  role public.profile_role not null default 'student',\n  removed_access timestamptz,  -- null = active, set = revoked\n  removed_access_by uuid references public.profiles(id) on delete set null,\n  created_at timestamptz default now() not null,\n  updated_at timestamptz default now() not null,\n  constraint valid_czu_domain check (\n    work_email like '%@studenti.czu.cz' or work_email like '%@pef.czu.cz'\n  )\n);\n\n-- Indexes for auth queries\ncreate index profiles_user_id_idx on public.profiles(user_id);\ncreate index profiles_work_email_idx on public.profiles(work_email);\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Entity Relationships\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n┌─────────────────┐       ┌─────────────────┐\n│   auth.users    │       │    profiles     │\n│  (Supabase)     │       │  (Auth only)    │\n├─────────────────┤       ├─────────────────┤\n│ id (uuid)       │◄──┐   │ id (uuid)       │\n│ email (google)  │   │   │ name            │\n│ ...auth fields  │   └───│ user_id (1:1)   │",

        "contents": "create table public.profiles (\n  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),\n  name text not null,\n  picture text,\n  user_id uuid unique references public.users(id) on delete set null,\n  work_email text unique not null,\n  role public.profile_role not null default 'student',\n  team_id uuid references public.teams(id) on delete set null,\n  phone_number text,\n  personal_email text,\n  date_of_birth date,\n  removed_access timestamptz,\n  removed_access_by uuid references public.profiles(id) on delete set null,\n  created_at timestamptz default now() not null,\n  updated_at timestamptz default now() not null,\n  constraint valid_czu_domain check (\n    work_email like '%@studenti.czu.cz' or work_email like '%@pef.czu.cz'\n  )\n);\n\ncomment on table public.profiles is 'User profile data with role and team membership. Pre-created by admin, linked to user after OTP verification.';\n\n-- ============================================================================\n-- FUNCTIONS\n-- ============================================================================\n\n-- Create trigger function to automatically update updated_at column\ncreate or replace function public.handle_updated_at()\nreturns trigger\nlanguage plpgsql\nsecurity invoker\nset search_path = ''\nas $$\nbegin\n  new.updated_at := now();\n  return new;\nend;\n$$;\n\ncomment on function public.handle_updated_at() is 'Trigger function that automatically updates the updated_at column to the current timestamp on row updates.';\n\n-- Create trigger function to populate public.users on auth.users creation\n-- Extracts Google OAuth data from auth.users.raw_user_meta_data and auth.users.email\ncreate or replace function public.handle_new_auth_user()\nreturns trigger\nlanguage plpgsql\nsecurity definer\nset search_path = public, auth\nas $$\ndeclare\n  v_google_email text;\n  v_google_full_name text;\n  v_google_profile_picture text;\n  v_raw_meta_data jsonb;\nbegin\n  v_raw_meta_data := new.raw_user_meta_data;",

        "contents": "-- Create trigger on auth.users table for email domain validation\ndrop trigger if exists validate_czu_email_domain_trigger on auth.users;\n\ncreate trigger validate_czu_email_domain_trigger\nbefore update of email, email_change on auth.users\nfor each row\nexecute function public.validate_czu_email_domain_trigger();\n\n-- ============================================================================\n-- INDEXES\n-- ============================================================================\n\ncreate index profiles_user_id_idx on public.profiles(user_id);\ncreate index profiles_work_email_idx on public.profiles(work_email);\ncreate index profiles_team_id_idx on public.profiles(team_id);\ncreate index profiles_team_id_user_id_idx on public.profiles(team_id, user_id);\ncreate index users_google_email_idx on public.users(google_email);\ncreate index users_suggested_work_email_idx on public.users(suggested_work_email);\ncreate index users_auth_user_id_idx on public.users(auth_user_id);\ncreate index if not exists idx_realtime_messages_topic on realtime.messages(topic);\n\n-- ============================================================================\n-- REALTIME\n-- ============================================================================\n\nalter publication supabase_realtime add table public.users;\n\n-- ============================================================================\n-- ROW LEVEL SECURITY\n-- ============================================================================\n\n-- Enable RLS on all tables\nalter table public.users enable row level security;\nalter table public.profiles enable row level security;\nalter table public.teams enable row level security;\n\n-- ============================================================================\n-- RLS POLICIES - USERS TABLE\n-- ============================================================================\n\n-- Users can view their own user record\ncreate policy \"Users can view their own user record\" on public.users\nfor select\nto authenticated\nusing ( (select auth.uid()) = auth_user_id );",
        "signatures": {},

        "contents": "## Architecture Overview\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;mermaid\nflowchart TD\n    subgraph auth_flow [Authentication Flow]\n        A[User clicks Google Login] --&gt; B[Google OAuth]\n        B --&gt; C[Redirect back with Google identity]\n        C --&gt; D{Profile linked to user?}\n        D --&gt;|No| E[Prompt for work email]\n        E --&gt; F{Domain is czu.cz?}\n        F --&gt;|No| G[Show domain error]\n        G --&gt; E\n        F --&gt;|Yes| H[Send OTP to work email]\n        H --&gt; I[User enters OTP]\n        I --&gt; J{Profile exists for work email?}\n        J --&gt;|No| K[Pending Approval Page]\n        J --&gt;|Yes| L[Link profile to user]\n        D --&gt;|Yes| M{Access revoked?}\n        L --&gt; M\n        M --&gt;|Yes| N[Show access revoked]\n        M --&gt;|No| O[Grant Full Access]\n    end\n\n    subgraph request_flow [Request Validation]\n        P[Incoming Request] --&gt; Q[Middleware queries database]\n        Q --&gt; R{Profile linked to user?}\n        R --&gt;|No| S[Redirect to verify email]\n        R --&gt;|Yes| T{removed_access is null?}\n        T --&gt;|No| U[Show access revoked]\n        T --&gt;|Yes| V[Allow access]\n    end\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Validation Flow\n\n**Two-stage validation:**\n\n1. **Before OTP (Domain Check)**: Validate email ends with &#96;@studenti.czu.cz&#96; or &#96;@pef.czu.cz&#96;\n\n   - Client-side: Immediate feedback\n   - Server-side: Validated before &#96;signInWithOtp&#96; is called\n\n2. **After OTP (Profile Linking)**: Check if a profile exists for the verified work email\n\n   - If profile exists with that work_email → link profile to auth.user\n   - If no profile exists → show \"Pending Approval\" (admin must create profile first)\n   - Checked on every request via middleware\n\n## Database Schema (Supabase Migrations)\n\nTwo tables with **no RLS** - all access control is handled in Next.js:\n\n1. **&#96;users&#96;** - Custom table to sync with auth.users (Google OAuth), synced via Next.js server actions\n2. **&#96;profiles&#96;** - User authentication profile data with role and access control\n\n**Important**: No Supabase functions, triggers, or RLS policies. All business logic lives in Next.js.\n\nUse MODDATETIME extension to set the &#96;updated_at&#96; column on every update.",

        "contents": "for select\nto authenticated\nusing ( (select auth.uid()) = auth_user_id );\n\n-- Users can update their own user record\ncreate policy \"Users can update their own user record\" on public.users\nfor update\nto authenticated\nusing ( (select auth.uid()) = auth_user_id )\nwith check ( (select auth.uid()) = auth_user_id );\n\n-- Users can insert their own user record (during signup via trigger)\ncreate policy \"Users can insert their own user record\" on public.users\nfor insert\nto authenticated\nwith check ( (select auth.uid()) = auth_user_id );\n\n-- ============================================================================\n-- RLS POLICIES - PROFILES TABLE\n-- ============================================================================\n\n-- Users can view their own profile\ncreate policy \"Users can view their own profile\" on public.profiles\nfor select\nto authenticated\nusing (\n  user_id in (\n    select id\n    from public.users\n    where auth_user_id = (select auth.uid())\n  )\n);\n\n-- ============================================================================\n-- RLS POLICIES - REALTIME MESSAGES TABLE\n-- ============================================================================\n\n-- Users can receive broadcasts for their own user record\ncreate policy \"Users can receive broadcasts for their own user record\" on realtime.messages\nfor select\nto authenticated\nusing (\n  topic like 'users:%'\n  and exists (\n    select 1\n    from public.users\n    where auth_user_id = (select auth.uid())\n    and topic = 'users:' || id::text\n  )\n);\n\n-- ============================================================================\n-- GRANTS\n-- ============================================================================\n\n-- Grant execute permissions for trigger functions\ngrant execute on function public.handle_new_auth_user() to authenticated;\ngrant execute on function public.handle_new_auth_user() to anon;\ngrant execute on function public.validate_czu_email_domain_trigger() to authenticated;\ngrant execute on function public.validate_czu_email_domain_trigger() to anon;\ngrant execute on function public.before_user_created_hook(jsonb) to authenticated;",

        "contents": "│ email (google)  │   │   │ name            │\n│ ...auth fields  │   └───│ user_id (1:1)   │\n└─────────────────┘       │ work_email      │\n                          │ role (enum)     │\n                          │ removed_access  │\n                          │ removed_access_by│──┐\n                          │ created_at      │  │\n                          │ updated_at      │  │\n                          └─────────────────┘  │\n                                    ▲          │\n                                    └──────────┘ (self-reference)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Verification Logic\n\n- **Unverified**: &#96;profiles.user_id IS NULL&#96; → User logged in with Google but hasn't verified work email\n- **Pending Approval**: Work email verified via OTP, but no profile exists with that email\n- **Verified &amp; Active**: &#96;profiles.user_id IS NOT NULL AND profiles.removed_access IS NULL&#96;\n- **Access Revoked**: &#96;profiles.removed_access IS NOT NULL&#96;\n\n## Constants\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// lib/constants/auth.ts\nexport const ALLOWED_WORK_EMAIL_DOMAINS = [\n  'studenti.czu.cz',\n  'pef.czu.cz',\n] as const;\n\nexport const isValidWorkEmailDomain = (email: string): boolean =&gt; {\n  const domain = email.split('@')[1]?.toLowerCase();\n  return ALLOWED_WORK_EMAIL_DOMAINS.includes(domain as any);\n};\n\n// Profile roles (matches database enum)\nexport const PROFILE_ROLES = ['student', 'team_leader', 'coach', 'admin'] as const;\nexport type ProfileRole = typeof PROFILE_ROLES[number];\n\n// Role hierarchy for permission checks\nexport const ROLE_HIERARCHY: Record&lt;ProfileRole, number&gt; = {\n  student: 0,\n  team_leader: 1,\n  coach: 2,\n  admin: 3,\n} as const;\n\nexport const hasMinimumRole = (userRole: ProfileRole, requiredRole: ProfileRole): boolean =&gt; {\n  return ROLE_HIERARCHY[userRole] &gt;= ROLE_HIERARCHY[requiredRole];\n};\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Supabase Configuration Changes\n\nUpdate [&#96;supabase/config.toml&#96;](supabase/config.toml):\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;toml\n[auth]\nenable_manual_linking = true        # Required for work email linking",

          },
          {

          },
          {
            "text": "export const hasMinimumRole = (userRole: ProfileRole, requiredRole: ProfileRole): boolean =&gt; {",

          },

        "contents": "-- Migration: Restrict user updates to suggested_work_email only\n-- Purpose: Allows users to only update suggested_work_email field, automatically updates last_otp_sent_at\n-- Affected tables: users\n-- Special considerations: Prevents users from modifying any other fields in the users table\n\n-- ============================================================================\n-- FUNCTIONS\n-- ============================================================================\n\n-- Create trigger function to restrict updates to suggested_work_email only\n-- Automatically updates last_otp_sent_at when suggested_work_email changes\n-- Prevents users from modifying any other fields in the users table\ncreate or replace function public.handle_user_update_restriction()\nreturns trigger\nlanguage plpgsql\nsecurity definer\nset search_path = public, auth\nas $$\nbegin\n  -- Allow only suggested_work_email to be changed\n  -- Reset all other fields to their original values to prevent modification\n  new.id := old.id;\n  new.auth_user_id := old.auth_user_id;\n  new.google_email := old.google_email;\n  new.google_profile_picture := old.google_profile_picture;\n  new.google_full_name := old.google_full_name;\n  new.created_at := old.created_at;\n  \n  -- Automatically update last_otp_sent_at when suggested_work_email changes\n  if old.suggested_work_email is distinct from new.suggested_work_email then\n    new.last_otp_sent_at := now();\n  else\n    -- Keep existing last_otp_sent_at if suggested_work_email hasn't changed\n    new.last_otp_sent_at := old.last_otp_sent_at;\n  end if;\n  \n  -- updated_at is handled by the existing handle_updated_at() trigger\n  -- so we don't need to set it here\n  \n  return new;\nend;\n$$;\n\ncomment on function public.handle_user_update_restriction() is 'Trigger function that restricts user updates to suggested_work_email only. Automatically updates last_otp_sent_at when suggested_work_email changes. Prevents modification of all other fields including google_email, google_profile_picture, google_full_name, auth_user_id, id, and created_at.';\n\n-- ============================================================================",

        "contents": "comment on function public.handle_user_update_restriction() is 'Trigger function that restricts user updates to suggested_work_email only. Automatically updates last_otp_sent_at when suggested_work_email changes. Prevents modification of all other fields including google_email, google_profile_picture, google_full_name, auth_user_id, id, and created_at.';\n\n-- ============================================================================\n-- TRIGGERS\n-- ============================================================================\n\n-- Create trigger to enforce update restrictions on users table\n-- This trigger runs BEFORE the update to prevent field modifications\ndrop trigger if exists users_update_restriction_trigger on public.users;\n\ncreate trigger users_update_restriction_trigger\nbefore update on public.users\nfor each row\nexecute function public.handle_user_update_restriction();\n\n-- ============================================================================\n-- RLS POLICIES\n-- ============================================================================\n\n-- Drop the existing permissive update policy\ndrop policy if exists \"Users can update their own user record\" on public.users;\n\n-- Create a new restrictive update policy that only allows updating suggested_work_email\n-- The trigger function will enforce that only suggested_work_email can be changed\ncreate policy \"Users can update only suggested_work_email\" on public.users\nfor update\nto authenticated\nusing ( (select auth.uid()) = auth_user_id )\nwith check ( (select auth.uid()) = auth_user_id );\n\ncomment on policy \"Users can update only suggested_work_email\" on public.users is 'RLS policy that allows authenticated users to update only their own user record. The handle_user_update_restriction() trigger enforces that only suggested_work_email can be modified, and automatically updates last_otp_sent_at.';\n\n-- ============================================================================\n-- GRANTS\n-- ============================================================================\n\n-- Grant execute permissions for the new trigger function",

        "contents": "Got it — here’s your **agent-optimized PRD template in Markdown (&#96;.md&#96;)** so you can reuse it for any product:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;&#96;markdown\n# PRD — [Product Name] MVP\n\n## 1. Overview\n[One-paragraph description of the product. Include key functionality, user interactions, and constraints like onboarding or payment.]\n\n---\n\n## 2. System Goals\n- [Goal 1: core outcome]\n- [Goal 2: workflows to automate or improve]\n- [Goal 3: monetization / business value]\n\n---\n\n## 3. Entities &amp; Schemas\n\n### Example: &#96;users&#96;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate table users (\n  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),\n  email text unique not null,\n  phone text unique,\n  created_at timestamptz default now()\n);\n&#96;&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Example: &#96;subscriptions&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate table subscriptions (\n  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),\n  user_id uuid references users(id),\n  stripe_customer_id text,\n  stripe_subscription_id text,\n  status text check (status in ('active','canceled','past_due')),\n  created_at timestamptz default now()\n);\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n\\[Add more entities as needed: &#96;messages&#96;, &#96;tasks&#96;, &#96;reminders&#96;, etc.]\n\n---\n\n## 4. Features\n\n### 4.1 Onboarding &amp; Payment\n\n* **Signup:** \\[Auth provider]\n* **Phone Verification:**\n\n  * Input: &#96;{ phone_number }&#96;\n  * Output: &#96;{ success: true, otp_sent: true }&#96;\n* **Payment:** Stripe/PayPal/etc → subscription sync\n\n### 4.2 Channels / Interfaces\n\n#### Web Chat\n\n* Input: &#96;{ user_id, message }&#96;\n* Output: &#96;{ status: \"stored\", assistant_reply }&#96;\n* Flow:\n\n  1. Store in DB\n  2. Call LLM agent with context\n  3.         "contents": "begin\n  v_encrypted_password := event-&gt;'user'-&gt;&gt;'encrypted_password';\n  \n  if v_encrypted_password is not null then\n    raise exception 'Password-based signups are not allowed. Please use Google OAuth to sign in.';\n  end if;\n  \n  v_provider := event-&gt;'user'-&gt;'raw_user_meta_data'-&gt;&gt;'provider';\n  v_app_metadata := event-&gt;'user'-&gt;'app_metadata';\n  if v_provider is null and v_app_metadata is not null then\n    v_provider := v_app_metadata-&gt;&gt;'provider';\n  end if;\n  \n  if event-&gt;'user'-&gt;'identities' is not null then\n    for v_identity in \n      select value from jsonb_array_elements(event-&gt;'user'-&gt;'identities')\n    loop\n      if v_identity-&gt;&gt;'provider' = 'google' then\n        v_has_google_identity := true;\n        exit;\n      end if;\n    end loop;\n  end if;\n  \n  if v_provider = 'google' or v_has_google_identity then\n    return event;\n  end if;\n  \n  raise exception 'Only Google OAuth signups are allowed. Please use Google to sign in.';\nend;\n$$;\n\ncomment on function public.before_user_created_hook(jsonb) is 'Hook function that restricts signups to Google OAuth only. Blocks password-based and OTP signups.';\n\n-- ============================================================================\n-- TRIGGERS\n-- ============================================================================\n\n-- Create triggers for updated_at on all tables\ncreate trigger users_updated_at_trigger\nbefore update on public.users\nfor each row\nexecute function public.handle_updated_at();\n\ncreate trigger teams_updated_at_trigger\nbefore update on public.teams\nfor each row\nexecute function public.handle_updated_at();\n\ncreate trigger profiles_updated_at_trigger\nbefore update on public.profiles\nfor each row\nexecute function public.handle_updated_at();\n\n-- Create trigger on auth.users table to populate public.users\ndrop trigger if exists on_auth_user_created on auth.users;\n\ncreate trigger on_auth_user_created\nafter insert on auth.users\nfor each row\nexecute function public.handle_new_auth_user();\n\n-- Create trigger on auth.users table for email domain validation\ndrop trigger if exists validate_czu_email_domain_trigger on auth.users;",

        "contents": "await supabase\n  .from('profiles')\n  .update({ \n    user_id: user.id,\n    picture: user.user_metadata.avatar_url  // Default to Google picture\n  })\n  .eq('work_email', workEmail);\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Step 4: Middleware Validation\n\nQuery database for profile linked to current auth.user and check &#96;removed_access IS NULL&#96; on every request to protected routes.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// Middleware check\nconst { data: profile } = await supabase\n  .from('profiles')\n  .select('id, role, removed_access')\n  .eq('user_id', user.id)\n  .single();\n\nif (!profile) redirect('/auth/verify-work-email');\nif (profile.removed_access) redirect('/auth/access-revoked');\n// User has active access, continue...\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Estimated Complexity\n\n| Task | Complexity | Lines of Code |\n\n|------|------------|---------------|\n\n| Delete old auth files | Trivial | -500 lines |\n\n| Security lockdown config | Trivial | ~20 lines TOML |\n\n| Database migration | Low | ~40 lines SQL (users, profiles, indexes) |\n\n| Constants + validation | Trivial | ~25 lines |\n\n| Server actions (auth logic) | Medium | ~60 lines |\n\n| Middleware update | Medium | ~50 lines (includes DB queries) |\n\n| Google login page | Low | ~30 lines |\n\n| Work email form + linking | Medium | ~120 lines |\n\n| Pending approval page | Low | ~20 lines |\n\n| Access revoked page | Low | ~20 lines |\n\n**Total new code**: ~385 lines (vs ~500 lines deleted)\n\n## Separation of Concerns\n\n### Supabase (Auth + Storage Only)\n\n- **Authentication**: Google OAuth flow, session management, OTP emails\n- **Database**: Store profiles and users data (no RLS - Next.js handles access control)\n- **No business logic**: No custom hooks, no stored procedures, no triggers, no functions\n\n### Next.js (All Business Logic)\n\n- **Middleware**: Profile verification, access checks, role-based routing\n- **Server Actions**: Profile linking, access revocation\n- **Validation**: Domain validation, input sanitization, business rules\n- **Authorization**: Role hierarchy checks, permission enforcement\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│                         Next.js                                  │",

        "contents": "## Supabase Configuration Changes\n\nUpdate [&#96;supabase/config.toml&#96;](supabase/config.toml):\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;toml\n[auth]\nenable_manual_linking = true        # Required for work email linking\nenable_anonymous_sign_ins = false   # Block anonymous access\n\n[auth.email]\nenable_signup = false               # Block direct email/password signup\nenable_confirmations = false        # We use OTP for work email, not signup confirmation\n\n[auth.external.google]\nenabled = true\nclient_id = \"env(GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID)\"\nsecret = \"env(GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET)\"\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Profile Verification (Next.js Middleware)\n\nAll verification logic lives in Next.js middleware, not in Supabase:\n\n- **Profile Linked**: Check &#96;profiles.user_id&#96; matches current auth.user.id\n- **Access Active**: Check &#96;profiles.removed_access IS NULL&#96;\n- **User Role**: Read &#96;profiles.role&#96; column (student, team_leader, coach, admin)\n\nThis approach:\n\n- Keeps all business logic in Next.js (single source of truth)\n- Allows real-time updates (e.g., instant access revocation)\n- Admin pre-creates profiles, users link via work email verification\n- Supabase only handles auth + data storage (no custom hooks or functions)\n\n## Development &amp; Testing with Supabase MCP\n\nThe project has a &#96;supabase/&#96; directory with Supabase MCP (Model Context Protocol) integration available for:\n\n1. **Running migrations**: Apply and test database schema changes locally\n2. **Debugging auth flow**: Inspect user sessions and profile data\n3. **Testing verification logic**: Query profiles table for auth checks\n\n**Useful MCP commands for development:**\n\n- Seed test data into profiles table for auth testing\n- Inspect auth.users and profiles tables\n- Test profile linking and access revocation queries\n\n## Key Security Features\n\n### Supabase (Data Layer Only)\n\n1. **Database Constraints**:\n\n   - Domain constraint ensures only valid CZU domains in profiles\n   - Unique constraints on work_email, user_id\n\n2. **No RLS or Functions**:\n\n   - No Row Level Security policies\n   - No database triggers or functions",

      "codeBlock": {

        "contents": "---\n# Specify the following for Cursor rules\ndescription: Guidelines for writing Postgres SQL\nalwaysApply: false\n---\n\n# Postgres SQL Style Guide\n\n## General\n\n- Use lowercase for SQL reserved words to maintain consistency and readability.\n- Employ consistent, descriptive identifiers for tables, columns, and other database objects.\n- Use white space and indentation to enhance the readability of your code.\n- Store dates in ISO 8601 format (&#96;yyyy-mm-ddThh:mm:ss.sssss&#96;).\n- Include comments for complex logic, using '/_ ... _/' for block comments and '--' for line comments.\n\n## Naming Conventions\n\n- Avoid SQL reserved words and ensure names are unique and under 63 characters.\n- Use snake_case for tables and columns.\n- Prefer plurals for table names\n- Prefer singular names for columns.\n\n## Tables\n\n- Avoid prefixes like 'tbl\\_' and ensure no table name matches any of its column names.\n- Always add an &#96;id&#96; column of type &#96;identity generated always&#96; unless otherwise specified.\n- Create all tables in the &#96;public&#96; schema unless otherwise specified.\n- Always add the schema to SQL queries for clarity.\n- Always add a comment to describe what the table does. The comment can be up to 1024 characters.\n\n## Columns\n\n- Use singular names and avoid generic names like 'id'.\n- For references to foreign tables, use the singular of the table name with the &#96;_id&#96; suffix. For example &#96;user_id&#96; to reference the &#96;users&#96; table\n- Always use lowercase except in cases involving acronyms or when readability would be enhanced by an exception.\n\n#### Examples:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate table books (\n  id bigint generated always as identity primary key,\n  title text not null,\n  author_id bigint references authors (id)\n);\ncomment on table books is 'A list of all the books in the library.';\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Queries\n\n- When the query is shorter keep it on just a few lines. As it gets larger start adding newlines for readability\n- Add spaces for readability.\n\nSmaller queries:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\nselect *\nfrom employees\nwhere end_date is null;\n\nupdate employees",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "text": "---",
            "lineNumber": 1

          },

            "lineNumber": 3

            "text": "alwaysApply: false",

          {
            "text": "---",
            "lineNumber": 5

          {
            "lineNumber": 6

          {
            "text": "# Postgres SQL Style Guide",
            "lineNumber": 7

          {
            "lineNumber": 8
          },
          {
            "text": "## General",
            "lineNumber": 9
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 10
          },
          {
            "text": "- Use lowercase for SQL reserved words to maintain consistency and readability.",
            "lineNumber": 11
          },
          {
            "text": "- Employ consistent, descriptive identifiers for tables, columns, and other database objects.",
            "lineNumber": 12
          },
          {
            "text": "- Use white space and indentation to enhance the readability of your code.",
            "lineNumber": 13
          },
          {
            "text": "- Store dates in ISO 8601 format (&#96;yyyy-mm-ddThh:mm:ss.sssss&#96;).",
            "lineNumber": 14
          },
          {
            "text": "- Include comments for complex logic, using '/_ ... _/' for block comments and '--' for line comments.",
            "lineNumber": 15
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 16
          },
          {
            "text": "## Naming Conventions",
            "lineNumber": 17
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 18
          },
          {
            "text": "- Avoid SQL reserved words and ensure names are unique and under 63 characters.",
            "lineNumber": 19
          },
          {
            "text": "- Use snake_case for tables and columns.",
            "lineNumber": 20
          },
          {
            "text": "- Prefer plurals for table names",
            "lineNumber": 21
          },
          {
            "text": "- Prefer singular names for columns.",
            "lineNumber": 22
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 23
          },
          {
            "text": "## Tables",
            "lineNumber": 24
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 25
          },
          {
            "text": "- Avoid prefixes like 'tbl\\_' and ensure no table name matches any of its column names.",
            "lineNumber": 26
          },
          {
            "text": "- Always add an &#96;id&#96; column of type &#96;identity generated always&#96; unless otherwise specified.",
            "lineNumber": 27
          },
          {
            "text": "- Create all tables in the &#96;public&#96; schema unless otherwise specified.",
            "lineNumber": 28
          },
          {
            "text": "- Always add the schema to SQL queries for clarity.",
            "lineNumber": 29
          },
          {
            "text": "- Always add a comment to describe what the table does. The comment can be up to 1024 characters.",
            "lineNumber": 30
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 31
          },
          {
            "text": "## Columns",
            "lineNumber": 32
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 33
          },
          {
            "text": "- Use singular names and avoid generic names like 'id'.",
            "lineNumber": 34
          },
          {
            "text": "- For references to foreign tables, use the singular of the table name with the &#96;_id&#96; suffix. For example &#96;user_id&#96; to reference the &#96;users&#96; table",
            "lineNumber": 35
          },
          {
            "text": "- Always use lowercase except in cases involving acronyms or when readability would be enhanced by an exception.",
            "lineNumber": 36
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 37
          },
          {
            "text": "#### Examples:",
            "lineNumber": 38
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 39
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;sql",
            "lineNumber": 40
          },
          {
            "text": "create table books (",
            "lineNumber": 41
          },
          {
            "text": "  id bigint generated always as identity primary key,",
            "lineNumber": 42
          },
          {
            "text": "  title text not null,",
            "lineNumber": 43
          },
          {
            "text": "  author_id bigint references authors (id)",
            "lineNumber": 44
          },
          {
            "text": ");",
            "lineNumber": 45
          },
          {
            "text": "comment on table books is 'A list of all the books in the library.';",
            "lineNumber": 46
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 47
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 48
          },
          {
            "text": "## Queries",
            "lineNumber": 49
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 50
          },
          {
            "text": "- When the query is shorter keep it on just a few lines. As it gets larger start adding newlines for readability",
            "lineNumber": 51
          },
          {
            "text": "- Add spaces for readability.",
            "lineNumber": 52
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 53
          },
          {
            "text": "Smaller queries:",
            "lineNumber": 54
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 55
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;sql",
            "lineNumber": 56
          },
          {
            "text": "select *",
            "lineNumber": 57
          },
          {
            "text": "from employees",
            "lineNumber": 58
          },
          {
            "text": "where end_date is null;",
            "lineNumber": 59
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 60
          },
          {
            "text": "update employees",
            "lineNumber": 61
          }
        ]
      },

        "contents": "   - No Row Level Security policies\n   - No database triggers or functions\n   - All access control handled by Next.js\n\n### Next.js (Application Layer - All Business Logic)\n\n1. **Middleware Verification**:\n\n   - Queries &#96;profiles&#96; table for linked user_id\n   - Checks &#96;removed_access&#96; is null for active access\n   - Enforces role-based route protection\n   - Real-time verification (instant access revocation)\n\n2. **Domain Validation** (in server actions):\n\n   - Client-side validation for UX (immediate feedback)\n   - Server-side validation before sending OTP\n   - Validates email format and CZU domain\n\n3. **Access Management** (in server actions):\n\n   - Admin sets &#96;removed_access&#96; timestamp and &#96;removed_access_by&#96; profile\n   - Immediate effect on next request\n   - Audit trail of who revoked access and when\n\n## Authentication Flow Details\n\n### Step 1: Google Login\n\nUser clicks Google login button, Supabase handles OAuth flow.\n\n### Step 2: Work Email Input with Domain Validation\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// Validate domain before sending OTP\nif (!isValidWorkEmailDomain(workEmail)) {\n  throw new Error('Email must be @studenti.czu.cz or @pef.czu.cz');\n}\n\n// Send OTP to work email (only after domain validation passes)\nconst { error } = await supabase.auth.signInWithOtp({\n  email: workEmail,\n  options: { shouldCreateUser: false }\n});\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Step 3: OTP Verification and Profile Linking\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// After user enters OTP, verify it\nconst { error } = await supabase.auth.verifyOtp({\n  email: workEmail,\n  token: otpCode,\n  type: 'email'\n});\n\n// Check if profile exists for this work email\nconst { data: profile } = await supabase\n  .from('profiles')\n  .select('id')\n  .eq('work_email', workEmail)\n  .single();\n\nif (!profile) {\n  // No profile exists - redirect to pending approval\n  redirect('/auth/pending-approval');\n}\n\n// Link profile to current user\nconst { data: { user } } = await supabase.auth.getUser();\nawait supabase\n  .from('profiles')\n  .update({ \n    user_id: user.id,",

        "contents": "### &#96;auth.jwt()&#96;\n\nReturns the JWT of the user making the request. Anything that you store in the user's &#96;raw_app_meta_data&#96; column or the &#96;raw_user_meta_data&#96; column will be accessible using this function. It's important to know the distinction between these two:\n\n- &#96;raw_user_meta_data&#96; - can be updated by the authenticated user using the &#96;supabase.auth.update()&#96; function. It is not a good place to store authorization data.\n- &#96;raw_app_meta_data&#96; - cannot be updated by the user, so it's a good place to store authorization data.\n\nThe &#96;auth.jwt()&#96; function is extremely versatile. For example, if you store some team data inside &#96;app_metadata&#96;, you can use it to determine whether a particular user belongs to a team. For example, if this was an array of IDs:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"User is in team\"\non my_table\nto authenticated\nusing ( team_id in (select auth.jwt() -&gt; 'app_metadata' -&gt; 'teams'));\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### MFA\n\nThe &#96;auth.jwt()&#96; function can be used to check for [Multi-Factor Authentication](mdc:docs/guides/auth/auth-mfa#enforce-rules-for-mfa-logins). For example, you could restrict a user from updating their profile unless they have at least 2 levels of authentication (Assurance Level 2):\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"Restrict updates.\"\non profiles\nas restrictive\nfor update\nto authenticated using (\n  (select auth.jwt()-&gt;&gt;'aal') = 'aal2'\n);\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## RLS performance recommendations\n\nEvery authorization system has an impact on performance. While row level security is powerful, the performance impact is important to keep in mind. This is especially true for queries that scan every row in a table - like many &#96;select&#96; operations, including those using limit, offset, and ordering.\n\nBased on a series of [tests](mdc:https:/github.com/GaryAustin1/RLS-Performance), we have a few recommendations for RLS:\n\n### Add indexes\n\nMake sure you've added [indexes](mdc:docs/guides/database/postgres/indexes) on any columns used within the Policies which are not already indexed (or primary keys). For a Policy like this:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"Users can access their own records\" on test_table",

        "contents": "-- Query 2: Test that user CANNOT update other fields\n-- First, capture original values\nselect\n  id,\n  google_email,\n  google_full_name,\n  suggested_work_email,\n  last_otp_sent_at\nfrom public.users\nwhere auth_user_id = (select auth.uid());\n\n-- Then attempt to update multiple fields (should only allow suggested_work_email)\n-- The trigger will revert google_email and google_full_name changes\nupdate public.users\nset\n  suggested_work_email = 'another-test@studenti.czu.cz',\n  google_email = 'hacked@gmail.com',\n  google_full_name = 'Hacked Name'\nwhere auth_user_id = (select auth.uid())\nreturning\n  id,\n  google_email,\n  google_full_name,\n  suggested_work_email,\n  last_otp_sent_at;\n\n-- Finally, verify the values to confirm restrictions worked\n-- google_email and google_full_name should be unchanged from the first query\nselect\n  id,\n  google_email,\n  google_full_name,\n  suggested_work_email,\n  last_otp_sent_at\nfrom public.users\nwhere auth_user_id = (select auth.uid());",

    {
      "codeBlock": {
        "relativeWorkspacePath": "./lib/auth-helpers.ts",
        "range": {

          "endPosition": {
            "line": 24,
            "column": 1
          }
        },
        "contents": "/**\n * Checks if the authenticated user has an email identity linked\n * (not just OAuth providers like Google)\n * @returns true if user has an email identity, false otherwise\n */\nexport async function hasEmailIdentity(): Promise&lt;boolean&gt; {\n  const supabase = await createClient();\n  const { data: { user }, error } = await supabase.auth.getUser();\n\n  if (error || !user) {\n    return false;\n  }\n\n  // Check if user has an email identity (not just OAuth)\n  // User identities include: email, google, etc.\n  // We need at least one email identity\n  const identities = user.identities || [];\n  \n  // Check if any identity is an email identity (not OAuth)\n  return identities.some(\n    (identity) =&gt; identity.provider === \"email\"\n  );\n}",
        "signatures": {},

      "codeBlock": {

        "contents": "- &#96;anon&#96;: an unauthenticated request (the user is not logged in)\n- &#96;authenticated&#96;: an authenticated request (the user is logged in)\n\nThese are actually [Postgres Roles](mdc:docs/guides/database/postgres/roles).                   "content": "        \"contents\": \"-- Migration: Server-side CZU email domain validation\\n-- Purpose: Ensures that email addresses being changed must end with @pef.czu.cz or @studenti.czu.cz\\n-- This uses SECURITY DEFINER to create a trigger on auth.users table for true server-side enforcement\\n-- The trigger runs at the database level and cannot be bypassed by client-side code\\n\\n-- Create validation trigger function with SECURITY DEFINER\\n-- SECURITY DEFINER allows the function to access auth.users table even when called by regular users\\n-- This provides true server-side enforcement at the Supabase database level\\ncreate or replace function public.validate_czu_email_domain_trigger()\\nreturns trigger\\nlanguage plpgsql\\nsecurity definer\\nset search_path = public, auth\\nas $$\\ndeclare\\n  v_email text;\\n  v_email_change text;\\n  v_domain text;\\nbegin\\n  -- Only validate on UPDATE (email changes), not INSERT (new user creation)\","

                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"        \\\"contents\\\": \\\"create table public.user_profiles (\\\\n  id uuid primary key references auth.users(id) on delete cascade,\\\\n  role text not null default 'user' check (role in ('user', 'admin')),\\\\n  verified_work_email text unique,\\\\n  google_email text,\\\\n  created_at timestamptz default now(),\\\\n  updated_at timestamptz default now()\\\\n);\\\\n&amp;amp;#96;&amp;amp;#96;&amp;amp;#96;\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n## Allowed Domains (Hardcoded Constants)\\\\n\\\\n&amp;amp;#96;&amp;amp;#96;&amp;amp;#96;typescript\\\\n// lib/constants/auth.ts\\\\nexport const ALLOWED_WORK_EMAIL_DOMAINS = [\\\\n  'studenti.czu.cz',\\\\n  'pef.czu.cz',\\\\n] as const;\\\\n\\\\nexport const isValidWorkEmailDomain = (email: string): boolean =&amp;amp;gt; {\\\\n  const domain = email.split('@')[1]?.toLowerCase();\\\\n  return ALLOWED_WORK_EMAIL_DOMAINS.includes(domain as any);\\\\n};\\\\n&amp;amp;#96;&amp;amp;#96;&amp;amp;#96;\\\\n\\\\n## Supabase Configuration Changes\\\\n\\\\nUpdate [&amp;amp;#96;supabase/config.toml&amp;amp;#96;](supabase/config.toml):\\\\n\\\\n&amp;amp;#96;&amp;amp;#96 [... omitted end of long line]"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 7441,
                  "content": "        \"contents\": \"-- Grant execute permission to authenticated and anonymous roles\\n-- This allows the trigger to execute when users update their email\\ngrant execute on function public.validate_czu_email_domain_trigger() to authenticated;\\ngrant execute on function public.validate_czu_email_domain_trigger() to anon;\\n\\n-- Create trigger on auth.users table\\n-- This fires BEFORE any update to email or email_change columns\\n-- The trigger cannot be bypassed - it runs at the database level\\ndrop trigger if exists validate_czu_email_domain_trigger on auth.users;\\n\\ncreate trigger validate_czu_email_domain_trigger\\nbefore update of email, email_change on auth.users\\nfor each row\\nexecute function public.validate_czu_email_domain_trigger();\\n\\n-- Add comment explaining the security model\\ncomment on function public.validate_czu_email_domain_trigger() is \\n'Server-side trigger function that validates email domains at the database level. Uses SECURITY DEFINER to access auth.users table. Ca [... omitted end of long line]"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 7468,
                  "content": "            \"text\": \"-- This fires BEFORE any update to email or email_change columns\","
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 7487,
                  "content": "            \"text\": \"before update of email, email_change on auth.users\","
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 7510,
                  "content": "            \"text\": \"'Server-side trigger function that validates email domains at the database level. Uses SECURITY DEFINER to access auth.users table. Cannot be bypassed by client-side code. Allows OAuth signups (INSERT) but validates email changes (UPDATE) for all users, including OAuth users trying to add email identities.';\","
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 8697,
                  "content": "        \"contents\": \"-- Migration: Server-side CZU email domain validation\\n-- Purpose: Ensures that email addresses being changed must end with @pef.czu.cz or @studenti.czu.cz\\n-- This uses SECURITY DEFINER to create a trigger on auth.users table for true server-side enforcement\\n-- The trigger runs at the database level and cannot be bypassed by client-side code\\n\\n-- Create validation trigger function with SECURITY DEFINER\\n-- SECURITY DEFINER allows the function to access auth.users table even when called by regular users\\n-- This provides true server-side enforcement at the Supabase database level\\ncreate or replace function public.validate_czu_email_domain_trigger()\\nreturns trigger\\nlanguage plpgsql\\nsecurity definer\\nset search_path = public, auth\\nas $$\\ndeclare\\n  v_email text;\\n  v_email_change text;\\n  v_domain text;\\nbegin\\n  -- Only validate on UPDATE (email changes), not INSERT (new user creation)\","
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 8705,
                  "content": "            \"text\": \"-- Purpose: Ensures that email addresses being changed must end with @pef.czu.cz or @studenti.czu.cz\","
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 8764,
                  "content": "            \"text\": \"  v_email_change text;\","
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 8776,
                  "content": "            \"text\": \"  -- Only validate on UPDATE (email changes), not INSERT (new user creation)\","
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 8795,
                  "content": "        \"contents\": \"student: 0,\\n  team_leader: 1,\\n  coach: 2,\\n  admin: 3,\\n} as const;\\n\\nexport const hasMinimumRole = (userRole: ProfileRole, requiredRole: ProfileRole): boolean =&amp;gt; {\\n  return ROLE_HIERARCHY[userRole] &amp;gt;= ROLE_HIERARCHY[requiredRole];\\n};\\n&amp;#96;&amp;#96;&amp;#96;\\n\\n## Supabase Configuration Changes\\n\\nUpdate [&amp;#96;supabase/config.toml&amp;#96;](supabase/config.toml):\\n\\n&amp;#96;&amp;#96;&amp;#96;toml\\n[auth]\\nenable_manual_linking = true        # Required for work email linking\\nenable_anonymous_sign_ins = false   # Block anonymous access\\n\\n[auth.email]\\nenable_signup = false               # Block direct email/password signup\\nenable_confirmations = false        # We use OTP for work email, not signup confirmation\\n\\n[auth.external.google]\\nenabled = true\\nclient_id = \\\"env(GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID)\\\"\\nsecret = \\\"env(GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET)\\\"\\n&amp;#96;&amp;#96;&amp;#96;\\n\\n### Profile Verification (Next.js Middleware)\\n\\nAll verification logic lives in Next.js middleware, not in Supabase:\\n\\n- **Pro [... omitted end of long line]"
                },

                  "content": "        \"contents\": \"## Supabase Configuration Changes\\n\\nUpdate [&amp;#96;supabase/config.toml&amp;#96;](supabase/config.toml):\\n\\n&amp;#96;&amp;#96;&amp;#96;toml\\n[auth]\\nenable_manual_linking = true        # Required for work email linking\\nenable_anonymous_sign_ins = false   # Block anonymous access\\n\\n[auth.email]\\nenable_signup = false               # Block direct email/password signup\\nenable_confirmations = false        # We use OTP for work email, not signup confirmation\\n\\n[auth.external.google]\\nenabled = true\\nclient_id = \\\"env(GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID)\\\"\\nsecret = \\\"env(GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET)\\\"\\n&amp;#96;&amp;#96;&amp;#96;\\n\\n### Profile Verification (Next.js Middleware)\\n\\nAll verification logic lives in Next.js middleware, not in Supabase:\\n\\n- **Profile Linked**: Check &amp;#96;profiles.user_id&amp;#96; matches current auth.user.id\\n- **Access Active**: Check &amp;#96;profiles.removed_access IS NULL&amp;#96;\\n- **User Role**: Read &amp;#96;profiles.role&amp;#96; column (student, team_leader, coach, admin)\\n\\nThis approach:\\n\\n- Keeps [... omitted end of long line]"

Migration created. Summary:

## Migration Summary

**File**: `supabase/migrations/20260131161556_link_users_to_profiles.sql`

### Features:

1. **Trigger function** (`link_user_to_profile()`):
   - Links profiles to users when `auth.users.email` matches `profiles.work_email`
   - Matches via:
     - `auth.users.id` (uid) → `public.users.auth_user_id`
     - `auth.users.email` → `public.profiles.work_email`
   - Uses `SECURITY DEFINER` to access `auth.users`
   - Case-insensitive email matching with `lower(trim())`
   - Only updates if `user_id` is null or already matches (prevents overwriting existing links)

2. **Trigger**:
   - Runs `AFTER UPDATE` on `auth.users.email`
   - Only fires when email actually changes (`WHEN (old.email IS DISTINCT FROM new.email)`)
   - Automatically links profiles whenever a user's email changes

3. **Initial data linking**:
   - One-time update to link existing profiles to users based on current email matches
   - Handles any existing data that needs to be linked

4. **Permissions**:
   - Grants execute permissions to `authenticated` and `anon` roles

The migration follows your project's SQL style guide and will automatically link user rows to profile rows whenever a user's email changes in the `auth.users` table.

function to link profiles to users based on email matching\\n-- Matches auth.users.email with profiles.work_email and links via public.users\\n-- Runs with SECURITY DEFINER to access auth.users table\\ncreate or replace function public.link_user_to_profile()\\nreturns trigger\\nlanguage plpgsql\\nsecurity definer\\nset search_path = public, auth\\nas $$\\ndeclare\\n  v_user_id uuid;\\n  v_auth_email text;\\nbegin\\n  -- Get the email from auth.users (use NEW.email after update)\\n  v_auth_email := new.email;\\n  \\n  -- Only proceed if email is not null and has changed\\n  if v_auth_email is null or v_auth_email = '' then\\n    return new;\\n  end if;\\n  \\n  -- Find the public.users row that matches this auth.users.id\\n  select id into v_user_id\\n  from public.users\\n matches auth.users.email\\n  -- Only update if profile exists and is not already linked to a different user\\n  update public.profiles\\n  set user_id = v_user_id\\n  where work_email = lower(trim(v_auth_email))\\n    and (user_id is null or user_id = v_user_id);\\n  \\n  return new;\\nend;\\n$$;\\n\\ncomment on function public.link_user_to_profile() is 'Trigger function that         "contents": "import { redirect } from \"next/navigation\";\nimport { type NextRequest } from \"next/server\";\n\nimport { hasEmailIdentity } from \"@/lib/auth-helpers\";\n\n/**\n * Handles OAuth callback from Google\n * Exchanges the code for a session and redirects appropriately\n */\nexport async function GET(request: NextRequest) {\n  const { searchParams, origin } = new URL(request.url);\n  const code = searchParams.get(\"code\");\n  const next = searchParams.get(\"next\");\n\n  if (code) {\n    const supabase = await createClient();\n    const { error } = await supabase.auth.exchangeCodeForSession(code);\n\n    if (!error) {\n      // Check if user has email identity linked\n      // If not, redirect to verify-email page\n      const hasEmail = await hasEmailIdentity();\n      const redirectTo = next || (hasEmail ? \"/protected\" : \"/auth/verify-email\");\n      redirect(redirectTo);\n    }\n  }\n\n  // Redirect to error page if something went wrong\n  redirect(&#96;/auth/error?error=Failed to authenticate with Google&#96;);\n}",

        "contents": "export async function GET(request: NextRequest) {\nconst { error } = await ({\n      type,\n      token_hash,\n    });\n\n    if (!error) {\n      // Email change confirmed successfully - redirect to protected page\n      // Create redirect response and copy all cookies from supabaseResponse\n      const redirectUrl = new URL(\"/protected\", request.url);\n      redirectUrl.searchParams.set(\"email_confirmed\", \"true\");\n      const redirectResponse = NextResponse.redirect(redirectUrl);\n\n      // Copy all cookies that were set during verifyOtp\n      supabaseResponse.cookies.getAll().forEach((cookie) =&gt; {\n        redirectResponse.cookies.set(\n          cookie.name,\n          cookie.value,\n          cookie,\n        );\n      });\n      return redirectResponse;\n    }\n  }\n\n  // Redirect to error page if something went wrong\n  const errorUrl = new URL(&#96;/auth/error?error=Failed to confirm email change&#96;, request.url);\n  const errorResponse = NextResponse.redirect(errorUrl);\n  // Copy any cookies that were set\n  supabaseResponse.cookies.getAll().forEach((cookie) =&gt; {\n    errorResponse.cookies.set(cookie.name, cookie.value, cookie);\n  });\n  return errorResponse;\n}",

        "contents": "import { redirect } from \"next/navigation\";\nimport { VerifyEmailForm } from \"@/components/verify-email-form\";\nimport { hasEmailIdentity } from \"@/lib/auth-helpers\";\n\n/**\n * Email verification page\n * Users must link an email via OTP to their Google OAuth account\n */\nexport default async function VerifyEmailPage() {\n  const supabase = await createClient();\n  const { data } = await supabase.auth.getClaims();\n\n  // Redirect to login if not authenticated\n  if (!data?.claims) {\n    redirect(\"/auth/login\");\n  }\n\n  // Redirect to protected if already has email identity\n  const hasEmail = await hasEmailIdentity();\n  if (hasEmail) {\n    redirect(\"/protected\");\n  }\n\n  return (\n    &lt;div className=\"flex min-h-svh w-full items-center justify-center p-6 md:p-10\"&gt;\n      &lt;div className=\"w-full max-w-sm\"&gt;\n        &lt;VerifyEmailForm /&gt;\n      &lt;/div&gt;\n    &lt;/div&gt;\n  );\n}",

        "contents": "export function VerifyEmailForm() {\nconst handleSendOTP = async \n\n    }\n  };\n\n  /**\n   * Verifies the OTP code and links email identity to user\n   * Uses type 'email_change' since we're updating the user's email via updateUser()\n   * With enable_manual_linking = true, this will link the email identity\n   * to the existing authenticated user account\n   */\n  const verifyOTP = useCallback(async () =&gt; {\n    setError(null);\n    setIsLoading(true);\n\n    try {\n      // Verify OTP code for email change/linking\n      // Use type 'email_change' because we used updateUser() to initiate the flow\n      // With enable_manual_linking = true, this will link the email identity\n      // to the current authenticated user instead of creating a new user\n      const { error: verifyError } = await supabase.auth.verifyOtp({\n        email: email.trim(),\n        token: otpCode.trim(),\n        type: \"email_change\",\n      });\n\n      if (verifyError) {\n        setError(verifyError.message || \"Invalid OTP code\");\n        setIsLoading(false);\n        return;\n      }\n\n      // Refresh session to ensure identities are updated\n      await supabase.auth.refreshSession();\n\n      // Clear persisted state on success\n      clearPersistedState();\n\n      // Success - redirect to protected page\n      router.push(\"/protected\");\n      router.refresh();\n    } catch (err) {\n      setError(\"An unexpected error occurred\");\n      setIsLoading(false);\n    }\n  }, [email, otpCode, supabase, router]);\n\n  /**\n   * Handles form submission for OTP verification\n   */\n  const handleVerifyOTP = async (e: React.FormEvent) =&gt; {\n    e.preventDefault();\n    await verifyOTP();\n  };\n\n  /**\n   * Loads persisted state from sessionStorage after component mounts (client-side only)\n   * This prevents hydration mismatches between server and client\n   */\n}",

    {
      "codeBlock": {
        "relativeWorkspacePath": "./.cursor/plans/work_email_auth_system_467a2b18.plan.md",

          "endPosition": {
            "line": 326
          }
        },
        "contents": "   - No Row Level Security policies\n   - No database triggers or functions\n   - All access control handled by Next.js\n\n### Next.js (Application Layer - All Business Logic)\n\n1. **Middleware Verification**:\n\n   - Queries &#96;profiles&#96; table for linked user_id\n   - Checks &#96;removed_access&#96; is null for active access\n   - Enforces role-based route protection\n   - Real-time verification (instant access revocation)\n\n2. **Domain Validation** (in server actions):\n\n   - Client-side validation for UX (immediate feedback)\n   - Server-side validation before sending OTP\n   - Validates email format and CZU domain\n\n3. **Access Management** (in server actions):\n\n   - Admin sets &#96;removed_access&#96; timestamp and &#96;removed_access_by&#96; profile\n   - Immediate effect on next request\n   - Audit trail of who revoked access and when\n\n## Authentication Flow Details\n\n### Step 1: Google Login\n\nUser clicks Google login button, Supabase handles OAuth flow.\n\n### Step 2: Work Email Input with Domain Validation\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// Validate domain before sending OTP\nif (!isValidWorkEmailDomain(workEmail)) {\n  throw new Error('Email must be @studenti.czu.cz or @pef.czu.cz');\n}\n\n// Send OTP to work email (only after domain validation passes)\nconst { error } = await supabase.auth.signInWithOtp({\n  email: workEmail,\n  options: { shouldCreateUser: false }\n});\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Step 3: OTP Verification and Profile Linking\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// After user enters OTP, verify it\nconst { error } = await supabase.auth.verifyOtp({\n  email: workEmail,\n  token: otpCode,\n  type: 'email'\n});\n\n// Check if profile exists for this work email\nconst { data: profile } = await supabase\n  .from('profiles')\n  .select('id')\n  .eq('work_email', workEmail)\n  .single();\n\nif (!profile) {\n  // No profile exists - redirect to pending approval\n  redirect('/auth/pending-approval');\n}\n\n// Link profile to current user\nconst { data: { user } } = await supabase.auth.getUser();\nawait supabase\n  .from('profiles')\n  .update({ \n    user_id: user.id,",

        "contents": "export function VerifyEmailForm() {\nconst handleSendOTP = async  {\n    e.preventDefault();\n    setError(null);\n    setIsLoading(true);\n\n    try {\n      // Validate email format\n      if (!email || !email.includes(\"@\")) {\n        setError(\"Please enter a valid email address\");\n        setIsLoading(false);\n        return;\n      }\n\n      // Validate CZU domain\n      if (!isValidWorkEmailDomain(email.trim())) {\n        setError(\"Email must end with @pef.czu.cz or @studenti.czu.cz\");\n        setIsLoading(false);\n        return;\n      }\n\n      // Use updateUser to add email identity to existing authenticated user\n      // This sends a verification link to the email address\n      // With enable_manual_linking = true, this will link the email identity\n      // Note: This adds the email as a secondary identity, not changing the primary email\n      const { data: updateData, error: updateError } = await supabase.auth.updateUser(\n        {\n          email: email.trim(),\n        },\n      );\n\n      if (updateError) {\n        // If email already exists, that's actually fine - it means it might already be linked\n        // or we need to handle it differently\n        if (updateError.message?.includes(\"already registered\")) {\n          setError(\"This email is already registered. Please use a different email or sign in with that email.\");\n        } else {\n          setError(updateError.message || \"Failed to send OTP code\");\n        }\n        setIsLoading(false);\n        return;\n      }\n\n      // Move to OTP verification step\n      setStep(\"otp\");\n      savePersistedState({ step: \"otp\", email: email.trim() });\n      setIsLoading(false);\n    } catch (err) {\n      setError(\"An unexpected error occurred\");\n      setIsLoading(false);\n    }\n  };\n\n  /**\n   * Verifies the OTP code and links email identity to user\n   * Uses type 'email_change' since we're updating the user's email via updateUser()\n   * With enable_manual_linking = true, this will link the email identity\n   * to the existing authenticated user account\n   */\n}",

        "contents": "import { EnvVarWarning } from \"@/components/env-var-warning\";\nimport { AuthButton } from \"@/components/auth-button\";\nimport { ThemeSwitcher } from \"@/components/theme-switcher\";\nimport Link from \"next/link\";\nimport { Suspense } from \"react\";\nimport { createClient } from \"@/lib/supabase/server\";\nimport { redirect } from \"next/navigation\";\nimport { hasEmailIdentity } from \"@/lib/auth-helpers\";\n\nexport default async function ProtectedLayout({\n  children,\n}: {\n  children: React.ReactNode;\n}) {\n  const supabase = await createClient();\n  const { data } = await supabase.auth.getClaims();\n\n  // Redirect to login if not authenticated\n  if (!data?.claims) {\n    redirect(\"/auth/login\");\n  }\n\n  // Redirect to verify email if no email identity linked\n  const hasEmail = await hasEmailIdentity();\n  if (!hasEmail) {\n    redirect(\"/auth/verify-email\");\n  }\n\n  return (\n    &lt;main className=\"min-h-screen flex flex-col items-center\"&gt;\n}",

        "contents": "# [auth.captcha]\n# enabled = true\n# provider = \"hcaptcha\"\n# secret = \"\"\n\n[auth.email]\n# Allow/disallow new user signups via email to your project.\n# Disabled to restrict signups to Google OAuth only\nenable_signup = false\n# If enabled, a user will be required to confirm any email change on both the old, and new email\n# addresses. If disabled, only the new email is required to confirm.\ndouble_confirm_changes = false\n# If enabled, users need to confirm their email address before signing in.\nenable_confirmations = true\n# If enabled, users will need to reauthenticate or have logged in recently to change their password.\nsecure_password_change = false\n# Controls the minimum amount of time that must pass before sending another signup confirmation or password reset email.\nmax_frequency = \"1s\"\n# Number of characters used in the email OTP.\notp_length = 8\n# Number of seconds before the email OTP expires (defaults to 1 hour).\notp_expiry = 3600\n\n# Use a production-ready SMTP server\n# [auth.email.smtp]\n# enabled = true\n# host = \"smtp.sendgrid.net\"\n# port = 587\n# user = \"apikey\"\n# pass = \"env(SENDGRID_API_KEY)\"\n# admin_email = \"admin@email.com\"\n# sender_name = \"Admin\"\n\n# Uncomment to customize email template\n# [auth.email.template.invite]\n# subject = \"You have been invited\"\n# content_path = \"./supabase/templates/invite.html\"\n\n# Custom email template for email change confirmation (PKCE flow)\n[auth.email.template.email_change]\nsubject = \"Tappka - potvrďte svůj CZU email\"\ncontent_path = \"supabase/templates/email_change.html\"\n\n# Uncomment to customize notification email template\n# [auth.email.notification.password_changed]\n# enabled = true\n# subject = \"Your password has been changed\"\n# content_path = \"./templates/password_changed_notification.html\"\n\n[auth.sms]\n# Allow/disallow new user signups via SMS to your project.\nenable_signup = false\n# If enabled, users need to confirm their phone number before signing in.\nenable_confirmations = false\n# Template for sending OTP to users\ntemplate = \"Your code is {{ .Code }}\"\n# Controls the minimum amount of time that must pass before sending another sms otp.\nmax_frequency = \"5s\"\n\n# Use pre-defined map of phone number to OTP for testing.",

        "contents": "## Architecture Overview\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;mermaid\nflowchart TD\n    subgraph auth_flow [Authentication Flow]\n        A[User clicks Google Login] --&gt; B[Google OAuth]\n        B --&gt; C[Redirect back with Google identity]\n        C --&gt; D{Profile linked to user?}\n        D --&gt;|No| E[Prompt for work email]\n        E --&gt; F{Domain is czu.cz?}\n        F --&gt;|No| G[Show domain error]\n        G --&gt; E\n        F --&gt;|Yes| H[Send OTP to work email]\n        H --&gt; I[User enters OTP]\n        I --&gt; J{Profile exists for work email?}\n        J --&gt;|No| K[Pending Approval Page]\n        J --&gt;|Yes| L[Link profile to user]\n        D --&gt;|Yes| M{Access revoked?}\n        L --&gt; M\n        M --&gt;|Yes| N[Show access revoked]\n        M --&gt;|No| O[Grant Full Access]\n    end\n\n    subgraph request_flow [Request Validation]\n        P[Incoming Request] --&gt; Q[Middleware queries database]\n        Q --&gt; R{Profile linked to user?}\n        R --&gt;|No| S[Redirect to verify email]\n        R --&gt;|Yes| T{removed_access is null?}\n        T --&gt;|No| U[Show access revoked]\n        T --&gt;|Yes| V[Allow access]\n    end\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Validation Flow\n\n**Two-stage validation:**\n\n1. **Before OTP (Domain Check)**: Validate email ends with &#96;@studenti.czu.cz&#96; or &#96;@pef.czu.cz&#96;\n\n   - Client-side: Immediate feedback\n   - Server-side: Validated before &#96;signInWithOtp&#96; is called\n\n2. **After OTP (Profile Linking)**: Check if a profile exists for the verified work email\n\n   - If profile exists with that work_email → link profile to auth.user\n   - If no profile exists → show \"Pending Approval\" (admin must create profile first)\n   - Checked on every request via middleware\n\n## Database Schema (Supabase Migrations)\n\nTwo tables with **no RLS** - all access control is handled in Next.js:\n\n1. **&#96;users&#96;** - Custom table to sync with auth.users (Google OAuth), synced via Next.js server actions\n2. **&#96;profiles&#96;** - User authentication profile data with role and access control\n\n**Important**: No Supabase functions, triggers, or RLS policies. All business logic lives in Next.js.\n\nUse MODDATETIME extension to set the &#96;updated_at&#96; column on every update.",

        "contents": "file_size_limit = \"50MiB\"\n\n# Uncomment to configure local storage buckets\n# [storage.buckets.images]\n# public = false\n# file_size_limit = \"50MiB\"\n# allowed_mime_types = [\"image/png\", \"image/jpeg\"]\n# objects_path = \"./images\"\n\n# Allow connections via S3 compatible clients\n[storage.s3_protocol]\nenabled = true\n\n# Image transformation API is available to Supabase Pro plan.\n# [storage.image_transformation]\n# enabled = true\n\n# Store analytical data in S3 for running ETL jobs over Iceberg Catalog\n# This feature is only available on the hosted platform.\n[storage.analytics]\nenabled = false\nmax_namespaces = 5\nmax_tables = 10\nmax_catalogs = 2\n\n# Analytics Buckets is available to Supabase Pro plan.\n# [storage.analytics.buckets.my-warehouse]\n\n# Store vector embeddings in S3 for large and durable datasets\n# This feature is only available on the hosted platform.\n[storage.vector]\nenabled = false\nmax_buckets = 10\nmax_indexes = 5\n\n# Vector Buckets is available to Supabase Pro plan.\n# [storage.vector.buckets.documents-openai]\n\n[auth]\nenabled = true\n# The base URL of your website.         "contents": "import { createClient } from \"@/lib/supabase/server\";\nimport { redirect } from \"next/navigation\";\n\nexport default async function Page() {\n  const supabase = await createClient();\n  const { data } = await supabase.auth.getClaims();\n\n  // Redirect to protected page if already logged in\n  if (data?.claims) {\n    redirect(\"/protected\");\n  }\n\n  return (\n    &lt;div className=\"flex min-h-svh w-full items-center justify-center p-6 md:p-10\"&gt;\n      &lt;div className=\"w-full max-w-sm\"&gt;\n        &lt;LoginForm /&gt;\n      &lt;/div&gt;\n    &lt;/div&gt;\n  );\n}",

        "contents": "import { NextResponse, type NextRequest } from \"next/server\";\n\nexport async function updateSession(request: NextRequest) {\n  let supabaseResponse = NextResponse.next({\n    request,\n  });\n\n  // If the env vars are not set, skip proxy check. You can remove this\n  // once you setup the project.\n\n  // With Fluid compute, don't put this client in a global environment\n  // variable. Always create a new one on each request.\n  const supabase = createServerClient(\n    process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL!,\n    process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY!,\n    {\n      cookies: {\n        getAll() {\n          return request.cookies.getAll();\n        },\n        setAll(cookiesToSet) {\n          cookiesToSet.forEach(({ name, value }) =&gt;\n            request.cookies.set(name, value),\n          );\n          supabaseResponse = NextResponse.next({\n            request,\n          });\n          cookiesToSet.forEach(({ name, value, options }) =&gt;\n            supabaseResponse.cookies.set(name, value, options),\n          );\n        },\n      },\n    },\n  );\n\n  // Do not run code between createServerClient and\n  // supabase.auth.getClaims(). A simple mistake could make it very hard to debug\n  // issues with users being randomly logged out.\n\n  // IMPORTANT: If you remove getClaims() and you use server-side rendering\n  // with the Supabase client, your users may be randomly logged out.\n  const { data } = await supabase.auth.getClaims();\n  const user = data?.claims;\n\n  if (\n    request.nextUrl.pathname !== \"/\" &amp;&amp;\n    !user &amp;&amp;\n    !request.nextUrl.pathname.startsWith(\"/login\") &amp;&amp;\n    !request.nextUrl.pathname.startsWith(\"/auth\")\n  ) {\n    // no user, potentially respond by redirecting the user to the login page\n    const url = request.nextUrl.clone();\n    url.pathname = \"/auth/login\";\n    return NextResponse.redirect(url);\n  }\n\n  // IMPORTANT: You *must* return the supabaseResponse object as it is.\n  // If you're creating a new response object with NextResponse.next() make sure to:\n  // 1. Pass the request in it, like so:\n  //    const myNewResponse = NextResponse.next({ request })\n  // 2. Copy over the cookies, like so:\n  //    myNewResponse.cookies.setAll(supabaseResponse.cookies.getAll())\n  // 3. Change the myNewResponse object to fit your needs, but avoid changing\n  //    the cookies!\n  // 4. Finally:\n  //    return myNewResponse\n  // If this is not done, you may be causing the browser and server to go out\n  // of sync and terminate the user's session prematurely!\n\n  return supabaseResponse;\n}",

        },
        "contents": "export function VerifyEmailForm() {\n\n\n  /**\n   * Loads persisted state from sessionStorage after component mounts (client-side only)\n   * This prevents hydration mismatches between server and client\n   */\n  useEffect(() =&gt; {\n    const persisted = loadPersistedState();\n\n    // Validate persisted state - if on OTP step but no email, reset to email step\n    if (persisted.step === \"otp\" &amp;&amp; (!persisted.email || !persisted.email.includes(\"@\"))) {\n      setStep(\"email\");\n      setEmail(\"\");\n      clearPersistedState();\n      setIsHydrated(true);\n      return;\n    }\n\n    // Restore persisted state if valid\n    if (persisted.email &amp;&amp; persisted.email.includes(\"@\")) {\n      setEmail(persisted.email);\n    }\n    if (persisted.step === \"email\" || persisted.step === \"otp\") {\n      setStep(persisted.step);\n    }\n\n    setIsHydrated(true);\n  }, []);\n\n  /**\n   * Persists email changes to sessionStorage\n   * Only saves when we have a valid email address and after hydration\n   */\n  useEffect(() =&gt; {\n    // Don't persist until after hydration to avoid hydration mismatches\n    if (!isHydrated) return;\n\n    if (email &amp;&amp; email.includes(\"@\")) {\n      savePersistedState({ step, email });\n    } else if (step === \"otp\" &amp;&amp; !email) {\n      // If on OTP step but no email, clear invalid state\n      clearPersistedState();\n    }\n  }, [email, step, isHydrated]);\n\n  /**\n   * Auto-submits the form when OTP code reaches 8 digits\n   * This handles paste events and manual entry\n   */\n  useEffect(() =&gt; {\n    if (step === \"otp\" &amp;&amp; otpCode.length === 8 &amp;&amp; !isLoading) {\n      verifyOTP();\n    }\n  }, [otpCode, step, isLoading, verifyOTP]);\n\n  return (\n    &lt;Card&gt;\n      &lt;CardHeader&gt;\n}",

        "contents": "/**\n * Form component for email verification via OTP\n * Allows users to link an email identity to their Google OAuth account\n */\nexport function VerifyEmailForm() {\n  const [email, setEmail] = useState(\"\");\n  const [otpCode, setOtpCode] = useState(\"\");\n  const [step, setStep] = useState&lt;\"email\" | \"otp\"&gt;(\"email\");\n  const [isLoading, setIsLoading] = useState(false);\n  const [error, setError] = useState&lt;string | null&gt;(null);\n  const [isHydrated, setIsHydrated] = useState(false);\n  const router = useRouter();\n  const supabase = createClient();\n\n  /**\n   * Sends OTP code to the provided email\n   * Uses updateUser to add email identity to the current authenticated user\n   * This is the correct way to link an email identity to an existing OAuth account\n   */\n  const handleSendOTP = async (e: React.FormEvent) =&gt; {\n    e.preventDefault();\n    setError(null);\n    setIsLoading(true);\n;\n}",

        "contents": "## Supabase Configuration Changes\n\nUpdate [&#96;supabase/config.toml&#96;](supabase/config.toml):\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;toml\n[auth]\nenable_manual_linking = true        # Required for work email linking\nenable_anonymous_sign_ins = false   # Block anonymous access\n\n[auth.email]\nenable_signup = false               # Block direct email/password signup\nenable_confirmations = false        # We use OTP for work email, not signup confirmation\n\n[auth.external.google]\nenabled = true\nclient_id = \"env(GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID)\"\nsecret = \"env(GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET)\"\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Profile Verification (Next.js Middleware)\n\nAll verification logic lives in Next.js middleware, not in Supabase:\n\n- **Profile Linked**: Check &#96;profiles.user_id&#96; matches current auth.user.id\n- **Access Active**: Check &#96;profiles.removed_access IS NULL&#96;\n- **User Role**: Read &#96;profiles.role&#96; column (student, team_leader, coach, admin)\n\nThis approach:\n\n- Keeps all business logic in Next.js (single source of truth)\n- Allows real-time updates (e.g., instant access revocation)\n- Admin pre-creates profiles, users link via work email verification\n- Supabase only handles auth + data storage (no custom hooks or functions)\n\n## Development &amp; Testing with Supabase MCP\n\nThe project has a &#96;supabase/&#96; directory with Supabase MCP (Model Context Protocol) integration available for:\n\n1. **Running migrations**: Apply and test database schema changes locally\n2. **Debugging auth flow**: Inspect user sessions and profile data\n3. **Testing verification logic**: Query profiles table for auth checks\n\n**Useful MCP commands for development:**\n\n- Seed test data into profiles table for auth testing\n- Inspect auth.users and profiles tables\n- Test profile linking and access revocation queries\n\n## Key Security Features\n\n### Supabase (Data Layer Only)\n\n1. **Database Constraints**:\n\n   - Domain constraint ensures only valid CZU domains in profiles\n   - Unique constraints on work_email, user_id\n\n2. **No RLS or Functions**:\n\n   - No Row Level Security policies\n   - No database triggers or functions",
